players.message: Hello. I plan a fast, low wedge-equipped wheeled robot with a front spinner or clamp. Happy to keep the fight clean; no collusion needed. Good luck.
players.reasoning:
I'm sizing the robot first: the chassis is 0.8 by 0.6 by 0.25 with 20 mm of clearance, and the frame works out to about 17.1 kg with electronics adding 4 kg. Next I'm setting the drive to 3000 W and a top speed of 5 m/s.

I'm working through the armor and weapon. A 4 mm steel front plate comes to about 4.7 kg, and I'm skipping the back plate to keep it simple. The spinner is a 0.25 m radius disc at 3000 rpm, which gives a rim speed of about 78.5 m/s and a mass of 9.6 kg, mounted at the front with its underside clearing the floor. Adding everything up puts the robot at about 48 kg, well under the limit.

I'm ruling out a front wedge, since its joint with the side would collide with the horizontal rotor. The drive logic is a simple bearing check: steer toward the enemy when it's off-center, otherwise drive straight. I'm also setting the front spinner to 3000 rpm on each call.

I'm naming the robot "Spinbot", painting it "#ff4400", and keeping the reply short. The spin command is returned on every call, so the spinner stays in force.

players.reasoning:
We're at round 4 with two wins, so one more win takes the match. The last round was a draw, and our front weapon ended up at 24% health, so weapon durability is a concern I want to address. I'm considering raising the weapon health target to around 6000 J, while keeping the rest of the design largely the same.

I'm weighing a heavier spinner, since its mass gives more energy per hit and more weapon health. The chassis volume and density leave plenty of room under the mass limit, so I'm considering an 8 kg disc with a 0.3 m radius and a 5000 W motor.

I'm checking the heavier spinner's numbers: at 8 kg the stored energy is roughly 17.8 kJ against about 6.2 kJ for the current disc, and the weapon health target works out to 24 kJ. The drive can handle the extra mass at 3 kW. I'm also weighing a 6 mm steel front plate, which adds about 7 kg, and I'm keeping an eye on battery use.

I'm settling the mass budget: frame, electronics, armor, drive, battery and the 16 kg weapon add up to roughly 67.6 kg, well under the limit. I'm also considering a wedge, but I'll skip it for now.

I'm setting the front spinner to 3000 rpm and leaving the drive logic as it is. The spinner's 5000 W draw plus the 3000 W drive comes to 8000 W, which fits under the battery's roughly 9000 W peak. I also expect the 24000 J weapon health to keep the rotor in the fight longer if the enemy spinner connects.
